sections.skill: Explain preapproval and calculate housing and total debt-to-income ratios

questions.prompt: The Lees receive a mortgage preapproval letter. What does it mean?

choices.text: Their loan is now guaranteed, no matter what changes in their finances or the home's value
They must buy a home within one week
A lender reviewed their finances and may lend up to an amount, subject to final approval
The seller must accept their offer

questions.correct_answer: A lender reviewed their finances and may lend up to an amount, subject to final approval
questions.intro: A preapproval is a lender's statement, after checking income, assets, and credit, of how much it may lend. Sellers take offers with preapproval more seriously. Final approval still depends on the home's appraisal, verified information, and no major changes in finances.
questions.feedback: Preapproval is conditional; final approval comes later.

misconceptions.A: Confuses a preapproval with guaranteed final approval

sources: CFPB: A preapproval is a lender's statement of how much it may lend after reviewing documents; it is not a final loan approval. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/whats-the-difference-between-a-prequalification-letter-and-a-preapproval-letter-en-127/)

questions.prompt: A lender uses a 28% guideline for housing costs. The Lees' gross monthly income is $8,000. What is the most housing payment (PITI) under that guideline?
questions.intro: Lenders look at debt-to-income (DTI). A common guideline: housing costs (PITI) ≤ about 28% of gross monthly income (the "front-end" ratio), and all monthly debt payments including housing ≤ about 36% (the "back-end" ratio). Actual limits vary by loan program.
sources: CFPB: A preapproval is a lender's statement of how much it may lend after reviewing documents; it is not a final loan approval. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/whats-the-difference-between-a-prequalification-letter-and-a-preapproval-letter-en-127/)

questions.prompt: Using the 36% total-debt guideline on $8,000 gross monthly income, and the Lees' $500 car payment and $300 student loan payment, what is the most they could spend on PITI?
questions.intro: Back-end limit: housing + other debt payments ≤ 36% of gross income. Housing allowed = 36% of income − other debt payments.
sources: CFPB: A preapproval is a lender's statement of how much it may lend after reviewing documents; it is not a final loan approval. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/whats-the-difference-between-a-prequalification-letter-and-a-preapproval-letter-en-127/)

questions.prompt: Which factor most improves the mortgage rate a borrower is offered?

choices.text: A higher offer on the house
A strong credit history and score

questions.correct_answer: A strong credit history and score
questions.intro: Lenders price mortgages by risk: credit score, down payment, DTI, and loan type all affect the rate.
questions.feedback: Better credit usually earns a lower rate.

misconceptions.A: Price does not set the rate
misconceptions.B: Not a rate factor by itself
misconceptions.C: Timing alone does not improve risk

questions.prompt: The Lees can afford $2,080 PITI. Taxes and insurance are $650 a month. How much is left for principal and interest?
questions.intro: To estimate a price range, subtract taxes and insurance from the PITI limit, then find what loan that principal-and-interest payment supports.

questions.prompt: At 6.5% for 30 years, each $1,000 borrowed costs about $6.32 a month. About how large a loan does a $1,430 payment support?
questions.intro: A payment factor gives the monthly cost per $1,000 borrowed. Loan supported ≈ payment ÷ factor × $1,000.
